# zenz model and llama.cpp runtime

**State in anmitsu 1.0.0.** The APK bundles two files in `assets/`, both pinned by SHA-256 in
`android/app/zenz-assets.lock`: the zenz-v3.2-xsmall Q5_K_M GGUF, unmodified, and `arm64-v8a/libastra_zenz.so`, built
from `android/zenz-native` and the unmodified llama.cpp v0.7.0 source (recipe below). Neither file is in the Git source.
The app loads them only after its CPU check (`android/app/src/main/java/dev/astra/ime/ZenzCpu.kt`); otherwise it converts
with the dictionary alone. No training or fine-tuning was done. Open licence questions are listed in
[THIRD-PARTY.md](../../THIRD-PARTY.md); how to obtain and build the files is in [BUILDING.md](../../BUILDING.md) section 4.

**Notices: the existing signed APK and the corrected source are not the same.**

- The existing signed 1.0.0 APK (SHA-256 `2f454398…`, unchanged) ships, for these files, only
  `zenz-LICENSE-Apache-2.0.txt` (from `Apache-2.0.txt` here), `llama.cpp-LICENSE.txt` and `llama.cpp-LICENSE-jsonhpp.txt`.
  None of its 13 notice files contains the Mozilla Foundation notice of llamafile sgemm or any CC BY-SA text or link.
- The source now also copies `zenz-MODEL-NOTICE.txt` (model attribution, CC BY-SA 4.0 as currently labelled upstream)
  and `llamafile-LICENSE.txt` (below) into `assets/licenses/`, and `scripts/package-android.ps1 -RequireZenz` requires
  both. A replacement signed distribution APK has not been prepared yet; the existing signed APK is unchanged, and any
  local unsigned build made for verification is separate from it. The model, the `.so` and their hashes are unchanged.

**llamafile sgemm.** The 1.0.0 library (`91a88be6…`) exports `llamafile_sgemm` (`llvm-nm -D -C`); the build cache has
`GGML_LLAMAFILE` on and Ninja compiles `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/llamafile/sgemm.cpp`. That file of llama.cpp tag `v0.7.0`
(https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/v0.7.0/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/llamafile/sgemm.cpp) begins with
"Copyright 2024 Mozilla Foundation" and the MIT permission notice and disclaimer; `llamafile-LICENSE.txt` carries that
copyright line with the standard MIT text. Whether other components compiled into the `.so` need notices of their own
has still not been checked one by one.

**YaRN and Unicode data (checked 2026-11-23, source headers only).** In llama.cpp `v0.7.0`,
`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp` (compiled into ggml-cpu for the native build) credits the YaRN algorithm at lines
6255–6256 to https://github.com/jquesnelle/yarn, whose LICENSE (MIT, Copyright (c) 2023 Jeffrey Quesnelle and Bowen
Peng) is copied verbatim as `yarn-LICENSE.txt`. That is the relation recorded; each symbol was not traced. The tables
in `src/unicode-data.cpp` were generated by `gen-unicode-data.py`, which reads UnicodeData.txt/PropList from
unicode.org and uses Python `unicodedata`; the normalization tables' comment names Unicode 16.0.0, while the version
used for the main tables is not pinned (the script fetches the latest). `Unicode-LICENSE.txt` is the official
https://www.unicode.org/license.txt (Unicode License V3), added as conservative attribution coverage; this does not
establish the tables' full provenance or that they are all Unicode 16.0.0. The source copies both into
`assets/licenses/` and `-RequireZenz` requires both. The earlier unsigned verification APK (`44259e3e…`) had 15
notice files; a candidate built from this source would have 17, which has not been built or checked yet. The existing
signed APK (`2f454398…`, 13 notice files) is unchanged.

**Licences.** anmitsu's own scorer and JNI code (`android/zenz-native`) is under the project's MIT licence
([LICENSE](../../LICENSE)). The zenz model keeps its own licence terms (labelling below) and llama.cpp/ggml keeps
MIT with its bundled notices; the project licence does not replace either. The open points (model training data,
notices for every llama.cpp component in the `.so`) concern the APK, which bundles both files, not the Git source,
which contains neither.

## Integration notes

- `android/zenz-native`: C++ scorer over the llama.cpp C API (`zenz_scorer.cpp`), a JNI bridge and a host CLI.
  llama.cpp is compiled from the pinned source without modification.
- The GGUFs declare the pre-tokenizer `gpt2-small-japanese-char`, unknown to upstream llama.cpp. The scorer
  overrides `tokenizer.ggml.pre` at load time (`kv_overrides`) and tokenizes one character at a time so each
  vocabulary character maps to one token (checked: 7 chars → 7 tokens). U+EE00–U+EE02 are not in the
  vocabulary and become byte tokens, as with the original byte-level tokenizer.
- `</s>` is looked up as the end token; the GGUF `eos_token_id` field points at another id.

## Building the Android library

No script does this. With NDK r30, CMake 4.4.4 and Ninja from the table above, in a short fresh directory (Ninja's incremental stat breaks over 260 characters on Windows):

```
cmake -S android/zenz-native -B <out> -G Ninja -DCMAKE_MAKE_PROGRAM=<ninja> -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=<ndk>/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake -DANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a -DANDROID_PLATFORM=android-26 \
  -DGGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH=armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16 -DLLAMA_DIR=<llama.cpp-0.7.0>
cmake --build <out> --target astra_zenz
llvm-strip --strip-unneeded <out>/libastra_zenz.so -o <dir>/arm64-v8a/libastra_zenz.so
```

Then put the new hash in `android/app/zenz-assets.lock`. Historical check (0.1.28): this recipe on the 0.1.5 scorer source reproduced the library locked for 0.1.5 to 0.1.27 (`82c60356…`) in every section and in all 1,016,755 disassembled lines,
with `GIT_EXE` pointed at a stub so that ggml's stamped commit is the old `1a82356`; only the build-id differs. Whether the 1.0.0 library (`91a88be6…`) is reproduced byte for byte on another machine has not been checked.

**`armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16` means the library needs those CPU features, while the app's minSdk is 26.** Loading it on a CPU without them would stop the process on an illegal instruction. Since 1.0.0 the app therefore loads it only in a 64-bit ARM process whose kernel reports every required feature (`ZenzCpu.kt`); on any other device, or when the answer cannot be read, it does not load the library and converts with the dictionary alone. Which phones lack the features was not checked.

The host build (`zenz-cache-check`, the JVM evaluation library) uses w64devkit, the same CMake call without the toolchain and ABI lines, `-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++ -DJAVA_HOME=<jdk>`.
`zenz-cache-check <model.gguf> [threads]` must print PASSED: scores may not depend on what the scorer did before. Run it after any change to `zenz_scorer.cpp` or llama.cpp.
